key_insight: Crystal VAEs spontaneously organize atom-wise latent representations by elemental family, enabling family-level control of generated compositions.
engineering_relevance: Family-level composition control can steer crystal discovery toward promising chemical regions without additional optimization such as reinforcement learning.
method: Identify elemental-family regions in a vanilla crystal VAE’s latent space.
Train a flow model with family-indexed source components and family-matched source–target pairs.
Use a user-defined family template to select the source component for each atom during generation.
evidence_signal: On MP-20 and MPTS-52, FamilySpace reports competitive generation performance and prescribed family-composition matching; selected templates increase the fraction of crystals predicted stable or metastable.
watch_item: Family-level control does not guarantee exact elemental composition or experimentally verified stability.
paper_title: FamilySpace: From Emergent Chemical Semantics to Controllable Crystal Generation
